note: Held-out-generator evaluation of the two Tier 1 checkpoints. Windows are mean-pooled per document; the max-pooled variant is recorded in the per-benchmark ood_*.json files and is not the primary number because max inflates FPR on long human documents. 'deployed' figures use the threshold fit on the in-distribution validation split at a 0.1% FPR budget, which is the only threshold available at deployment time. 'fnr_at_budget' refits the threshold on the benchmark itself to hit 0.1% FPR there; it is optimistic and is reported only so the two arms can be compared at a matched operating point.

significance.method: paired bootstrap over documents, 10,000 resamples; both arms score the same documents, so documents rather than scores are resampled and both arms are recomputed on each resample

reading: The AUROC headline is not uniform. It is large on HC3, small on MAGE, and absent on RAID, where the sign reverses in 72.7% of resamples and the two arms are tied.

At a matched 0.1% false-positive budget the mirror arm has the lower FNR on all three benchmarks: 0.9295 vs 0.9695 on HC3, 0.9780 vs 0.9825 on MAGE, 0.7570 vs 0.8135 on RAID. That is the claim the data supports.
Neither arm is deployable out of distribution. At the deployed threshold both miss 63% to 96% of AI text, against 0.43% to 0.72% in distribution.
